summary: Configured a DNSSEC-signed authoritative `infra.test` zone with node1 primary, node2/node3 secondaries, and node4 using both secondaries. Authenticated updates, propagation, and one-server failover were successfully exercised.
actions_performed: Installed and enabled BIND; opened DNS through firewalld on authoritative nodes.
Generated a protected HMAC-SHA256 update key on node1 and enabled inline ECDSAP256SHA256 signing.
Persisted both secondary resolvers in node4’s NetworkManager profile.
Verified signed dynamic-update propagation and rejection of unsigned updates.
Stopped node2, demonstrated automatic resolution through node3, then restored and verified node2.
Removed the temporary update-proof record and confirmed final serial 2026090106 on both secondaries.

evidence.requirement: Authoritative primary/secondary topology and required records
evidence.summary: The three enabled authorities have valid role-specific configurations; both secondaries serve final serial 2026090106 with app=10.100.135.10 and status=ready.
BIND cryptographically verified final serial 2026090106 as fully signed with ECDSAP256SHA256; both secondaries serve RRSIGs.

evidence.requirement: Authenticated updates from node1 propagate to both secondaries
evidence.summary: A TSIG-signed update from node1 was approved and propagated at matching serial to both secondaries, while an unsigned update was refused. Authenticated cleanup also propagated successfully.
NetworkManager persistently lists node2 and node3 as node4’s resolvers; direct and system-resolver queries return the required signed records through both.

evidence.requirement: Resolution remains available if one authoritative server is unavailable
evidence.summary: After a healthy baseline, node2 was stopped with port 53 absent. node4 timed out against node2, automatically answered through node3 with valid app/status/RRSIG data, and node2 was then restored and verified synchronized.
